abstract: Mitochondrial ATP synthase is the main source of cellular ATP. Its assembly into dimers and oligomers is modulated by several subunits. While subunits e and g promote dimerization, DAPIT (USMG5) stabilizes dimer-dimer interactions. Whether DAPIT (diabetes associated protein in insulin-sensitive tissues) also controls ATP synthase function remained unknown. Using high-resolution live-cell imaging, metabolic profiling, mass spectrometry, and molecular genetics methods, we show that DAPIT-dependent dimer stabilization delays enzyme turnover and optimizes ATP synthesis. This structural role extends beyond bioenergetics: by coupling mitochondrial energy conversion to metabolic restructuring, DAPIT enables the upregulation of glycolysis and efficient shunting of substrates toward oxidative phosphorylation. This allows cells to sustain energy metabolism without activating stress responses. Our findings establish DAPIT as a molecular link between ATP synthase architecture and metabolic adaptation, with implications for understanding mitochondrial remodeling in proliferating and differentiating cells.
